--- title: "Funding relevant for getting a postdoc" format: html editor: source engine: knitr execute: eval: false --- ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.justify} # Other lists like this one Some other lists that Shikhara occasionally refers to. There is also EcoEvoJobs and EvolDir for more general searches.
  • [Dieter Lukas' list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1J2M_tQgoqV4ivpfEClh9qs9f2KQN2O1G3Jpda2aoHfQ/edit?gid=0#gid=0) of post-doc positions (biology wide)
  • [Allison Barner's list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1cHkWrbvNrRdhJL9Z8ucgBZ2HSts2GPA_yozbQPl_x_8/edit?gid=0#gid=0) of EEB focused positions
# Grants Some particular grants for very early post-docs that Shikhara finds enticing. Many of the Institutes of Advanced Study offer fellowships, I do not list those (apart from WiKo below).
  • The Walter Benjamin Grant and Fellowship from the DFG. Note that the stuff you are allowed to apply for depends on whether you finished the majority of your high school etc education in Germany. Mostly for research within Germany.
  • The Marie Curie Fellowships for post-docs in the EU.
  • The JSPS fellowships for post-docs in Japan. At most 2 years.
  • The EMBO fellowships for 2 year post-docs within the EU.
  • The WIKO fellowships for very short-term post-docs in Berlin.
  • The Santa Fe Institute fellowships to do interdisciplinary work in Santa Fe in the US.
# Resources: Grant applications, research proposals, etc Some grant applications etc that Shikhara thinks are insightful for how to structure applications.
  • [Collection of successful job applications in biology](https://github.com/RILAB/statements) compiled by Jeffrey Ross-Ibarra.
  • [Collection of successful NSF GRFP applications in EEB](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13ex9ykvReOQQSzMjEo9ur89BA_SfRBat4UrEDeiPw2A/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true) by Yaniv Brandvain. NEF GRFP is a USA based fellowship for early PhDs.
  • The [Open Grants Project](https://www.ogrants.org/grants-01-all), which collates many grant applications (mostly USA based).
  • Some [targeted resources and guidance on post-doc applications](https://zenodo.org/records/13235632) and how to structure CVs and cover letters for them. From EMBL. This is a 24 page PDF, so fairly detailed.
:::
